To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Global 500 companies have made little effort to address privacy concerns.

1) 68.5% of Global 50 Web sites have no privacy policies, 2) 31.5% of the Global 50 do have privacy policies, 3) 30% of the 50 have comprehensive policies, 4) 70% do not have comprehensive policies, and 5) 52% of those with policies have policies that do not include all four elements of the notice, choice, access and data security dimensions of privacy.

1) 68% of the Global 250 companies have privacy policies; 2) only 38% of the Global companies provide a privacy seal; 3) the Global companies are not consistent in providing the four privacy principles (notice, choice/opt-out, access, and security) on their web sites; and, 4) there is no significant difference in the use of privacy policies among the Global 500 companies based on their country of origin.
